title: [CQ-R10d1] Guest MCP stdio shim
description:
Objective: give an in-guest agent CLI its only route to Moe. That route is a stdlib Python MCP stdio server. It maps MCP tools/call onto CQ-R08c bridge request frames over the agent socket (/run/moe/agent.sock), and only for the role's allowlisted tools.

Split from CQ-R10d (task-90847011) on 2026-10-29. Human decisions in the architect REPL: the CLI binaries come from a host pinned cache through a copy-only stream (CQ-R10d2/R10d3), and the CLIs run with full access inside the VM (CQ-R10d4). This slice depends on nothing unlanded.

Contract:
- A new scripts/local-runner/guest-mcp-shim.py: python3 -I, standard library only, LF line endings.
  - guest-bootstrap.mjs buildUserData installs it at /opt/moe/bin/moe-mcp-shim, root:root 0555.
  - Beside it goes a generated tools.json, root 0444: the role -> tool -> argument-keys table from guest-bridge.mjs TOOLS.
  - R07 readiness probes the sha256 of both files, and a mismatch is a readiness failure code.
- MCP stdio protocol (newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0):
  - initialize, with protocol-version negotiation, capabilities {tools: {}} and serverInfo;
  - notifications/initialized and ping;
  - tools/list: exactly the MOE_ROLE's allowlisted tools, each with an inputSchema built from its argument keys and additionalProperties false;
  - tools/call: argument keys must be within the allowlist. The shim sends {kind:'request', id, tool, args} as a length-prefixed frame on the agent socket, and answers with the response's result or a fixed error.
  - Any other method or message gets a JSON-RPC error with fixed text.
- Bounds:
  - a stdin line has a maximum size;
  - frames stay within guest-bridge.mjs's MAX_GUEST_FRAME_BYTES and MAX_HOST_FRAME_BYTES;
  - in-flight requests are bounded, with a per-call timeout;
  - errors are fixed codes and never echo guest text.
- The shim connects only to the fixed socket path. It never opens a network socket, and reads no environment variable except MOE_ROLE.
- Tests go in a NEW scripts/tests/local-runner-agents.test.mjs, which every later CQ-R10d slice extends. Each row uses a python3 -I -B importlib harness and a fake socket peer, and skips on win32 with a reason. Add the file to the CI local-runner step's file list, appended at the end of the run line (local-runner-bundle.test.mjs pins its prefix).

Out of scope: the CLI binaries (CQ-R10d2, R10d3), the argv, prompt and MCP config (CQ-R10d4), host session changes, and any verified-local or isolation claim.

Verification command (fresh, exit 0 required): node --test scripts/tests/local-runner.test.mjs scripts/tests/local-runner-agents.test.mjs (on WSL: env -i with the nvm Node 24 PATH).
definitionOfDone: tools/list returns exactly the MOE_ROLE's allowlisted tools, and an unknown or missing role serves none. A drift test compares the generated tools.json with guest-bridge.mjs TOOLS. Shown by tests.

tools/call reaches Moe only as a bridge request frame on the agent socket, and only for allowlisted tools and argument keys. Any other call, an oversized line or frame, or a malformed message gets a fixed JSON-RPC error. Shown by tests.
buildUserData installs the shim root:root 0555 and tools.json root 0444, and readiness fails on a hash mismatch of either. Shown by tests.
The CI local-runner step runs scripts/tests/local-runner-agents.test.mjs, and the verification command exits 0 with its output supplied to complete_task.
taskRails: No direct .moe edits; no Git-write commands by agents; wrappers own landing.
Do not enable verified-local or claim isolation until all requisite implementation and certification gates pass.

CQ-R10d1 (task-9faf1ef30b0a4264b6dccce1e7bf5b1d) may contain at most 650 changed lines (additions plus deletions by git diff --numstat, comments and blank lines included) across exactly scripts/local-runner/guest-mcp-shim.py (new), scripts/local-runner/guest-mcp-tools.json (new), scripts/local-runner/guest-bootstrap.mjs, scripts/local-runner/guest-readiness.mjs, scripts/tests/local-runner.test.mjs, scripts/tests/local-runner-agents.test.mjs (new) and .github/workflows/ci.yml. implementationPlan.description:
Shim protocol core, the generated tools.json, the new test file and its CI line. Covers DoD 1, DoD 2 except the relay, and the CI half of DoD 4.

1. scripts/local-runner/guest-mcp-tools.json. GENERATE it; never hand-edit it. From the repo root:
`node --input-type=module -e "import { writeFileSync } from 'node:fs'; import { TOOLS } from './scripts/local-runner/guest-bridge.mjs'; writeFileSync('scripts/local-runner/guest-mcp-tools.json', JSON.stringify(Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(TOOLS).map(([role, tools]) => [role, Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(tools).map(([tool, entry]) => [tool, entry.args]))]))) + '\n')"`
- Result: one compact line of role -> tool -> argument keys, in TOOLS order.
- Why checked in: guest-bridge.mjs imports guest-bootstrap.mjs, so bootstrap importing TOOLS would create an ESM cycle. SH1 pins the file to TOOLS byte for byte.

2. scripts/local-runner/guest-mcp-shim.py (new).
- Format: line 1 is `#!/usr/bin/python3 -I`; LF only; standard library only.
- Header comment: this is the in-guest agent CLI's only route to Moe; the protocol source of truth is CQ-R08c's agent socket plus guest-bridge.mjs; the host's scopeRequest stays the enforcement point; no isolation claim; verified-local stays unavailable.

Module constants:
- AGENT_SOCKET = '/run/moe/agent.sock'; TOOLS_PATH = '/opt/moe/bin/tools.json'.
- MAX_GUEST_FRAME_BYTES = 262144 and MAX_HOST_FRAME_BYTES = 4194304, with a 'mirrors guest-bridge.mjs' comment.
- MAX_LINE_BYTES = 262144.
- MAX_TOOLS_BYTES = 262144, equal to guest-bootstrap.mjs MAX_SUPERVISOR_BYTES, the asset bound.
- MAX_IN_FLIGHT = 8 (the supervisor's per-connection bound); MAX_REQUEST_ID = 2147483647.
- CALL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 120, above the host's 60 s forward cap.
- PROTOCOL_VERSIONS = ('2025-11-25', '2025-06-18', '2025-03-26', '2024-11-05'), newest first.
- TOOL and CODE regexes copied from guest-supervisor.py; KEY = [A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,63}.
- Read limits and paths from module globals at use time, never through default arguments, so the harness can lower them.

ERRORS is the only source of error text. Each entry is a JSON-RPC code plus a fixed message, and no message ever includes input:
- PARSE -32700 'Parse error.'
- INVALID_REQUEST -32600 'Invalid request.'
- TOO_LARGE -32600 'Request too large.'
- METHOD -32601 'Method not found.'
- INVALID_PARAMS -32602 'Invalid params.'
- TOOL_DENIED -32602 'Tool not available to this role.'
- ARGUMENT_DENIED -32602 'Argument not allowed for this tool.'
- BUSY -32001 'Too many tool calls in flight.'
- TIMEOUT -32002 'The tool call timed out.'
- UNAVAILABLE -32003 'The Moe bridge is unavailable.'
- REFUSED -32004 'Moe refused the tool call.' This one alone carries data {code: <the host's CODE>}.
PARSE, INVALID_REQUEST and the oversized-line TOO_LARGE always answer with id null. Every other error echoes the request id.

Functions:
- load_tools(path): read at most MAX_TOOLS_BYTES+1 bytes; parse as strict UTF-8 JSON. The result must be an object of role -> object of TOOL-matching name -> list of unique KEY-matching strings. Anything else, a missing file included, returns {} (serves none).
- serve(role, table, socket_path, timeout=None, in_fd=0, out_fd=1) returns the exit code. timeout None means CALL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS. The role's tools are table[role] only when role is a str key of table; otherwise none.
- main() = serve(os.environ.get('MOE_ROLE'), load_tools(TOOLS_PATH), AGENT_SOCKET), with the globals read at call time; then `if __name__ == '__main__': sys.exit(main())`. It reads no other environment variable.

stdin:
- Newline-delimited messages, read in chunks through a selectors loop; step 2 adds the socket to the same loop.
- A line over MAX_LINE_BYTES bytes before its newline gets ONE TOO_LARGE, and its bytes are discarded through the next newline, so the buffer never holds more than MAX_LINE_BYTES.
- Whitespace-only lines are ignored.
- EOF returns 0 and drops an unterminated final line. A stdout write failure returns 74 (os.EX_IOERR).
- Each reply is one line: json.dumps(separators=(',', ':'), ensure_ascii=True, allow_nan=False) + '\n', written whole through an os.write loop.

Parsing:
- Strict UTF-8 decode, then json.loads with parse_constant and parse_float hooks that refuse NaN, Infinity and non-finite floats such as 1e999.
- ValueError or RecursionError gives PARSE.
- The message must be an object with jsonrpc == '2.0' and a str method. A batch array, anything else, or an invalid id gives INVALID_REQUEST.
- A valid id is an int (not bool) with |id| < 2**53, or a str of at most 256 chars.
- A message without an id is a notification and is never answered: notifications/initialized, notifications/cancelled and any other.
- params, when present, must be an object, else INVALID_PARAMS.

Methods:
- initialize: params.protocolVersion must be a str, else INVALID_PARAMS. Answer it back when it is in PROTOCOL_VERSIONS, otherwise PROTOCOL_VERSIONS[0]. Include capabilities {tools: {}} and serverInfo {name: 'moe-guest-shim', version: '1'}. There is no initialize state machine.
- ping: {}.
- tools/list: {tools: [...]} in table order. Each entry is {name, inputSchema: {type: 'object', properties: {<key>: {} for each key}, additionalProperties: false}}.
- tools/call: a name that is not a str gives INVALID_PARAMS; a name outside the role's tools gives TOOL_DENIED. arguments (absent means {}) must be an object, else INVALID_PARAMS, and each of its keys must be in the tool's list, else ARGUMENT_DENIED. Other params keys such as _meta are ignored. Until step 2, an allowed call answers UNAVAILABLE.
- Any other method gives METHOD.

3. scripts/tests/local-runner-agents.test.mjs (new; every later CQ-R10d slice extends it). Reuse the patterns of local-runner-bridge.test.mjs:
- NO_GUEST = process.platform === 'win32' && '<reason>', as each Python row's skip.
- The LOAD importlib prelude, and spawn('python3', ['-I', '-B', '-c', LOAD + code, SHIM, ...args]). The -B flag keeps __pycache__ out of the bundled directory.
- A client helper writes JSON lines, collects stdout lines, ends stdin and asserts exit 0.
- A fake-peer helper: net.createServer on a short mkdtemp socket path (macOS caps AF_UNIX paths at 104 bytes) that records connections and frames.
- Every async row gets timeout: 30_000.

Rows:
- SH1 (DoD 1; its JS part also runs on win32). The guest-mcp-tools.json text equals the generator's TOOLS projection plus '\n'. Python part:
  - For worker and qa, tools/list returns TOOLS[role]'s names in order, each with the exact inputSchema.
  - For MOE_ROLE absent, '', 'admin', 'WORKER' and 'constructor', the list is [] and tools/call moe.get_context gives TOOL_DENIED.
  - load_tools returns {} for: a missing file, non-JSON, a non-object, a bad tool name, a non-list, duplicate keys, a bad key, and MAX_TOOLS_BYTES+1 bytes.
- SH2:
  - initialize echoes each supported version and answers an unknown one with '2025-11-25'.
  - capabilities and serverInfo are exactly as specified; ping gives {}.
  - After notifications/initialized and notifications/cancelled, the next stdout line is the answer to the following ping.
- SH3 (DoD 2's refusals). Each case gets its exact {code, message} and id, and the fake peer sees zero connections:
  - an unknown tool, and the other role's tool;
  - taskId, workerId and unknown argument keys;
  - non-object arguments, and non-object params;
  - initialize without a str protocolVersion;
  - an unknown method;
  - malformed JSON, invalid UTF-8, a UTF-8 BOM, NaN and 1e999;
  - a batch array, a non-object message, and a wrong jsonrpc;
  - ids 1.5, true, null, an object, and a 257-char string.
  A marker string is injected into method, tool and argument names, and no stdout line may contain it.
- SH4 (DoD 4, also on win32). The run line of ci.yml's 'Test local runner prerequisite bundles' step still starts with the prefix that local-runner-bundle.test.mjs pins, and ends with scripts/tests/local-runner-agents.test.mjs.

4. .github/workflows/ci.yml: append ` scripts/tests/local-runner-agents.test.mjs` to the end of that run line. Nothing else changes; CQ-V04b1 later appends after it.

implementationPlan.description:
Socket relay for tools/call (DoD 2), plus the shim's static and main() row.

Error handling: every failure of the socket, the frames, stdin or stdout maps to one fixed ERRORS entry, or to exit code 0 or 74. No exception escapes serve(), and every refusal is tested.

Connection:
- Opened lazily by the first allowed call: socket.socket(socket.AF_UNIX, socket.SOCK_STREAM).
- Connect to socket_path blocking, bounded by sock.settimeout(5), then switch to non-blocking and register in the same selector as stdin.
- Name the instance sock, never socket, and catch OSError, never socket.timeout. SH8 pins the socket.* attribute set.
- A connect failure answers that call UNAVAILABLE. There is no retry loop; the next call tries once more.

Frames:
- Exactly {'kind': 'request', 'id': n, 'tool': name, 'args': arguments}, encoded like guest-supervisor.py encode_frame: json.dumps(separators=(',', ':'), ensure_ascii=False, allow_nan=False), UTF-8 with backslashreplace, and a 4-byte big-endian length.
- A body over MAX_GUEST_FRAME_BYTES gives TOO_LARGE, and nothing is queued.
- n comes from one monotonic counter that starts at 1, is never reused and never exceeds MAX_REQUEST_ID.
- Frames go to an outbox that is drained only on EVENT_WRITE; never use a blocking send or sendall. Why: the supervisor stops reading a connection while replies are queued for it (Bridge.watch). A shim blocked in a send while its own receive buffer fills would deadlock.

Calls:
- At most MAX_IN_FLIGHT pending. The next call beyond that gets BUSY, and no frame is sent.
- Each pending call has a time.monotonic() deadline, and the select timeout is the nearest one. An expired call gets TIMEOUT and leaves pending.

Responses:
- recv in 65536-byte chunks. The 4-byte length must be 1..MAX_HOST_FRAME_BYTES, checked before any body byte is buffered. The body is strict UTF-8 JSON, refusing non-finite numbers.
- The frame must be exactly {kind: 'response', id: int, ok: true, result: object} or {kind: 'response', id: int, ok: false, error: {code: CODE}}.
- A pending id answers its JSON-RPC id. ok true returns the result unchanged; ok false returns REFUSED with data {code}.
- A non-pending id below the counter is a late reply to an expired call and is ignored.
- Anything else is a violation and gets the same handling: an id never assigned, a malformed frame or length, EOF, or an OSError. The connection closes, every pending call gets UNAVAILABLE, and the next call reconnects.

Rows. The fake peer decodes frames with createFrameDecoder(MAX_GUEST_FRAME_BYTES) plus parseGuestFrame and answers with encodeFrame({...}, MAX_HOST_FRAME_BYTES), or with raw bytes.
- SH5 (relay):
  - The worker's tools/call moe.start_step {stepId} reaches the peer as exactly {kind: 'request', id: 1, tool, args}, and the peer's ok result comes back unchanged as the JSON-RPC result.
  - ok:false {code: 'BRIDGE_UPSTREAM_FAILED'} gives REFUSED with that data.
  - Absent arguments forward {}.
  - A string JSON-RPC id is echoed.
  - Two calls answered in reverse order each get their own result.
- SH6 (bounds):
  - A line of exactly MAX_LINE_BYTES bytes is parsed. MAX_LINE_BYTES+1 gets one TOO_LARGE, and the next line is still served.
  - With m.MAX_GUEST_FRAME_BYTES lowered in the harness, a body of exactly the limit is sent; limit+1 gets TOO_LARGE and no frame.
  - Eight unanswered calls are relayed and the ninth gets BUSY with no frame. After the peer answers one, a new call is relayed.
  - Paused peer: while the peer does not read (pause()), a call with a frame near MAX_GUEST_FRAME_BYTES stays queued and a following ping is still answered. After resume() the frame arrives whole. This row kills a sendall mutant.
  - With timeout=0.3, an unanswered call gets TIMEOUT. The peer then answers it late and, after that, answers one more call. Stdout is then exactly [TIMEOUT, that call's result].
- SH7 (bridge failures):
  - No socket file, and a path with no listener, each give a prompt UNAVAILABLE.
  - The peer closing the connection while a call is pending gives UNAVAILABLE.
  - Each of these peer replies gives UNAVAILABLE for the pending call and closes the connection, and the next call opens a new connection and succeeds: a length header of 0; MAX_HOST_FRAME_BYTES+1; an id never assigned; an extra key; ok true with error; a lowercase or non-str code; a non-object result; an invalid UTF-8 body.
- SH8 (static and main()):
  - The file starts with the shebang and contains no CR byte.
  - Its imports are stdlib-only, by the bridge tests' IMPORT_ROOTS AST walk.
  - The socket.* attributes it uses are exactly ['AF_UNIX', 'SOCK_STREAM', 'socket'], collected the way I6 collects them.
  - The only environment access is os.environ.get('MOE_ROLE'). The AST check finds no other environ, environb, getenv or putenv reference.
  - A harness sets m.TOOLS_PATH to the repo tools.json, sets MOE_ROLE=qa plus decoy MOE_* variables, and replaces m.socket.socket with a recorder whose connect records (family, type, address) and raises FileNotFoundError. Running m.main(): tools/list gives the qa tools, a tools/call gives UNAVAILABLE, and the recorder holds exactly [(AF_UNIX, SOCK_STREAM, '/run/moe/agent.sock')].

Cleanup: an after() hook SIGKILLs every shim still running, closes every fake server and removes the temp dirs. Without it, a failing row leaves node --test hanging.

implementationPlan.description:
Bootstrap install and readiness hashes (DoD 3).

Error handling: a missing, empty or oversized asset throws the fixed BOOTSTRAP_ASSET_INVALID. A wrong owner, mode or digest on the guest is a readiness failure code, never an exception.

guest-bootstrap.mjs:
- GUEST_LAYOUT gains shim: '/opt/moe/bin/moe-mcp-shim' and shimTools: '/opt/moe/bin/tools.json'. It stays frozen.
- MESSAGES gains BOOTSTRAP_ASSET_INVALID: 'A bundled guest asset was missing or invalid.'
- A private readAsset(name) runs readFileSync(new URL(`./${name}`, import.meta.url)) inside a try/catch, then requires validPayload(bytes, MAX_SUPERVISOR_BYTES); otherwise it throws BOOTSTRAP_ASSET_INVALID. Call it only from buildUserData, never at import: platform-linux.mjs imports this module on the `cli.mjs doctor` path.
- buildUserData keeps its input {supervisor, credential}, validated first. It then reads guest-mcp-shim.py and guest-mcp-tools.json.
- write_files order: supervisor 0500, then the shim (root:root, '0555', at GUEST_LAYOUT.shim), then tools (root:root, '0444', at GUEST_LAYOUT.shimTools), then the credential 0400. The credential stays last.
- buildUserData returns the frozen {userData, supervisorSha256, shimSha256, shimToolsSha256}.
- Update the header comment.

guest-readiness.mjs:
- LAYOUT_PATHS appends GUEST_LAYOUT.shim and GUEST_LAYOUT.shimTools. EXACT_MODES adds '555:-r-xr-xr-x' and '444:-r--r--r--' for them.
- hashFailure becomes a factory, digestFailure(file, key, failure). supervisorHash keeps its id, argv and code.
- Two new CHECKS go right after supervisorHash:
  - shimHash: ['sudo', '-n', 'sha256sum', GUEST_LAYOUT.shim], failing with SHIM_HASH_MISMATCH.
  - shimToolsHash: the same on GUEST_LAYOUT.shimTools, failing with SHIM_TOOLS_HASH_MISMATCH.
- validInputs requires all three bootstrap digests to be lowercase 64-hex. boundaryFailures passes the three digests to the evaluators.
- waitForGuestReady's return shape is unchanged.
- Update the header comment.

scripts/tests/local-runner.test.mjs, CQ-R07 section only. Retain every test.
- EXPECTED_PROBES: add the two paths to the layout argv, and add the two probes after supervisorHash.
- LAYOUT: append 'root:root:555:-r-xr-xr-x:/opt/moe/bin/moe-mcp-shim' and 'root:root:444:-r--r--r--:/opt/moe/bin/tools.json' at the end, so every index-based withLine row stays valid.
- healthy(): answer the two new probes from BOOTSTRAP.
- Probe count: 6 + 15 * IDENTITIES.length.
- The GUEST_LAYOUT deepEqual gets the new keys.
- The buildUserData deepEqual expects the two new write_files entries and the two digests. Compute them from readFileSync of the repo files, never pasted base64, so CQ-R10d5's tools.json change needs no edit here.
- New rows:
  - LAYOUT_INVALID: shim mode 755, shim owned by ubuntu, tools mode 644, tools mode 666.
  - Each new probe's exact code (SHIM_HASH_MISMATCH or SHIM_TOOLS_HASH_MISMATCH) for another digest, another path, or a failed sha256sum.
  - BOOTSTRAP_INPUT_INVALID before any provider call for a missing or uppercase shimSha256 or shimToolsSha256.

scripts/tests/local-runner-agents.test.mjs, row SH9 (also on win32):
- buildUserData's decoded write_files entries for both paths have owner root:root, permissions '0555' or '0444', and content equal to the repo bytes. The returned digests are their sha256.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: An in-guest agent CLI reaches Moe only through /opt/moe/bin/moe-mcp-shim, a stdlib Python MCP stdio server (newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0). The shim serves exactly MOE_ROLE's allowlisted tools from the generated /opt/moe/bin/tools.json. It relays each allowed tools/call as one CQ-R08c bridge request frame on /run/moe/agent.sock and answers with the host's result, or with a fixed JSON-RPC error that never echoes input. Lines, frames, in-flight calls and call time are bounded. buildUserData installs the shim (root:root 0555) and tools.json (root 0444). R07 readiness verifies their modes and sha256. executionReady stays false and verified-local stays unavailable.
acceptanceCriteria: tools/list returns exactly TOOLS[MOE_ROLE]'s names and argument keys (inputSchema type object, an empty schema per key, additionalProperties false). An absent, empty or unknown role serves none, and the checked-in guest-mcp-tools.json is byte-equal to the TOOLS projection.

An allowed tools/call sends exactly one {kind:'request', id, tool, args} frame on the agent socket and returns the host result unchanged; a refusal returns REFUSED with data {code}. Every refused call, oversized line or frame, malformed message and unknown method gets its fixed JSON-RPC error, and no frame is sent.

Bounds: lines are at most MAX_LINE_BYTES; frames sent are at most MAX_GUEST_FRAME_BYTES; frames received are at most MAX_HOST_FRAME_BYTES; at most 8 calls are in flight; each call times out. A late reply is ignored. A protocol violation closes the connection and fails every pending call.
The shim opens only an AF_UNIX stream to the fixed socket path, reads only the MOE_ROLE environment variable, imports only stdlib modules, and starts with #!/usr/bin/python3 -I.

The user-data writes the shim at '0555' and tools.json at '0444', both root:root. Readiness fails with SHIM_HASH_MISMATCH or SHIM_TOOLS_HASH_MISMATCH on a digest mismatch, and with LAYOUT_INVALID on a wrong owner or mode.
The CI local-runner step runs scripts/tests/local-runner-agents.test.mjs, and the verification command exits 0.
invariants: executionReady is always false and verified-local stays unavailable; no isolation claim.
The host's scopeRequest stays the enforcement point. The shim is a convenience adapter and adds no trust.
No error text from the shim contains input. Only REFUSED carries data, and that data is the host's CODE-matching code.

The shim never blocks on a send, never opens a non-AF_UNIX socket, never connects anywhere except the path it is given (AGENT_SOCKET from main), and never reads an environment variable other than MOE_ROLE.
Every CQ-R07 test is retained. The supervisorHash probe, its argv and its code are unchanged. The credential stays the last write_files entry.
